requirements.text: Preserve the Duroflex identity and authentic product appearance; do not rebrand the product into another look.
Use the supplied de-stress/reset framing as the execution lens; do not swap in a different brand story.
Keep claims product-specific and substantiated; strategy decks and public copy are context, not proof of efficacy or performance.
Build scenes as calm, warm, human domestic spaces; avoid spa, clinic, showroom, or warehouse cues.
Keep red controlled and the information hierarchy simple so the product and message stay easy to read.
Retouch naturally and preserve texture, shadows, and believable physical contact.
Treat strategy and deck language as context only; verify final portfolio, claims, and identity masters before production.

preferences.text: Warm neutrals with depth, tactile materials, and natural light feel most aligned with the strongest supplied references.
Generous breathing space and a calm centered product read best across the supplied worlds.
Reading, reclining, turning, conversation, and small rituals feel more authentic than posed selling.
Category moods can flex by product: brighter for sleep, warmer for sofas and motion, intimate warm-tech for recovery, close tactile views for accessories.
Controlled red accents and integrated greenery feel more on-brand than full red rooms or scattered décor.

visualRules.value: The logo should identify the brand with confidence and restraint.
Use clean sans-serif hierarchy; headlines breathe and proof stays ordered.
Use one hero visual, one hero message, one brand cue, and one CTA.
Use Duroflex red as punctuation and identification only; do not flood rooms or backgrounds with red.
Keep rooms quiet, warm, human, and domestic; use natural materials, open space, integrated greenery, and soft light.
Show believable rest and release: closed eyes, soft hands, real stretch, calm connection; avoid presenter poses and forced smiles.
Avoid starbursts, heavy badges, excess CTAs, over-red backgrounds, and competing claims.
Retouch naturally; preserve fabric texture, skin truth, daylight variation, and natural shadows; reduce clutter and harsh reflections.
For sleep and mattress assets, keep a fresh, breathable feel; avoid hotel rooms, clouds, sleeping-couple clichés, medical blue overload, and layer explosions.
For recovery and massager assets, keep the setting intimate, precise, and warm-tech rather than clinical, isolated, or sci-fi dark.
Retail should feel like a calmer home, not a mattress warehouse, wellness spa, or clinical space.
Keep science simple and readable; avoid busy diagrams, too many icons, and medical fear.

preserve: natural materials, soft light, and believable use
explore: Morning reset, evening exhale, and focused recovery as category moods
Retail as a calmer home with consultative zones and unwind nooks
Compact connected home, garden-threshold reset, and filtered-light room families
avoid: Hotel, spa, clinic, showroom, or warehouse tropes
Over-red rooms, theatrical sets, busy wallpaper, and glossy clutter
Forced smiles, presenter poses, and performing comfort
Starbursts, heavy badges, excess CTAs, and competing claims
Floating products in darkness, black-box gadget staging, and artificial blur or fades
Unsupported medical, cortisol, pain-relief, or recovery claims
unknowns: Final logo wordmark, lockup, and approved typography
Adopted portfolio architecture and range migration map
Exact hero SKU/variant and product-specific claim boundary
Mechanism clearances, dimensions, and compatibility details
Complete social, paid-media, and video evidence
Whether the draft serif look or clean hierarchy is the final production master
guide.decisionSummary: Execute within the supplied de-stress/reset world: calm domestic spaces, controlled red, believable everyday use, and simple hierarchy. Keep claims product-specific and unresolved identity or portfolio details flagged until approved masters are confirmed.
